title: Steps Against Israel’s Pharma and Continuing Horrors in the West Bank
author: Daniel Warner
content:
![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/09/TevaCanada7-680x450.jpg)

Photograph Source: Raysonho @ Open Grid Scheduler / Scalable Grid Engine -CC0

Going to the pharmacy is always full of anxiety. It is not a pleasure to pick
up medicines to cure some health problems. It has now become easier for me to
go to my local pharmacy since my wife and I convinced the pharmacist to offer
clients generic drugs instead of Mepha products from Teva. And it appears that
more and more clients in Geneva and Switzerland are boycotting Mepha/Teva
drugs, if possible. It is our small effort, but it is far from stopping the
horrors in the West Bank, as reported by former Israeli military and
government officials as well as the U.S. ambassador to Israel.

The pharmaceutical industry is an important part of Israel’s economy. And
trying to get pharmacy customers to boycott its products is a small step
against Israel’s genocidal policies. Israel’s GDP was $540 billion in 2024.
Pharmaceutical exports were about $1.8 billion that year; they are not a huge
share of GDP, but they are an important export business for a country the size
of Israel.

Mepha and Teva have more than 330 products in Switzerland and sold about 25
million medicine packages in 2025, making their combined operation the leading
medicine supplier in Switzerland. Their presence in the Swiss market is hard
to ignore.

And it is what makes the pharmacy boycott possible. You don't have to boycott
some obscure Israeli product that nobody has heard of. Mepha is sitting on the
shelves of many ordinary Swiss pharmacies.

There has been a small Swiss campaign against Mepha/Teva, intensifying in
2026. It includes an appeal to Geneva pharmacists to stop advertising and
selling Mepha products where possible as well as an open letter directed to
Geneva and Swiss health authorities calling for reduced dependence on Teva. In
May and June, the Geneva boycott campaign reported pickets outside pharmacies,
the distribution of around 500 flyers and more than 1,000 boycott stickers.
The boycott campaign admitted that it had not established a method of
measuring the campaign’s impact before launching it.

Fighting companies like Mepha/Teva in Switzerland and the pharma lobby — like
fighting Swiss banks — is not simple. The pharmaceutical lobby is very well
represented in Swiss political and regulatory circles.

In 2022, the magazine _Public Eye_ identified 40 members of the Swiss National
Council (House of Representatives) and Council of States (Senate) who had a
direct connection to the pharmaceutical industry and/or health insurers. In
2025, _Public Eye_ identified 239 people who had moved between the
pharmaceutical industry and Swissmedic or the Federal Office of Public Health
(FOPH), including 173 connected to Swissmedic and 66 to the FOPH. Of the 741
people _Public Eye_ identified as having worked at Swissmedic, 294 — almost
40% — had previously worked for at least one pharmaceutical company.

Switzerland is not simply a country selling Israeli drugs. It has its own
powerful pharmaceutical industry, its own pharmaceutical lobby and a
regulatory system in which people move between the companies and the
institutions responsible for regulating them. When I asked my local pharmacist
why an association of pharmacies didn’t jointly stop supplying Mepha, he just
shrugged, recognizing the limits of what can be done.

But there has been progress. After speaking to the pharmacist several times
about selling Mepha/Teva products and encouraging the pharmacy to indicate
generic substitutes instead, my wife brought up the fact that the official
pharmacy car had Mepha printed on its side. Just last week, after I asked, the
pharmacist proudly said, “The Mepha sign is no longer on the pharmacy’s car.”

Removing the Mepha sign from the pharmacy car is a very small step. What the
former Israeli generals and officials saw in the West Bank shows how much more
needs to be done.

A recent _New York Times_ article reported their reactions. “This, what the
settlers are doing here, is the real threat to Israel,” Maj. Gen. Eyal Ben
Reuven said. “This is more concerning to me than Iran, Gaza or Lebanon.”

“This is ethnic cleansing, to put it simply,” a retired brigadier general and
former minister of health declared.

“Once a society behaves this way it is doomed,” a retired Air Force general
observed.

“I’m ashamed of what our people are doing here,” a retired Air Force general
confessed.

As for civil society protests, follow the courageous Israeli and Palestinian
“Combattants for Peace” in Stephen Apkon’s dramatic film “There is Another
Way.”

Even the U.S. ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, has publicly condemned
Israeli settler violence in the West Bank. In August 2026, during the siege of
Palestinian homes in Qusra, he called the settlers involved “terrorists” and
said their actions went beyond ordinary criminal behavior.

On September 5, 2026, Huckabee visited Turmus Ayya in the West Bank, met
Palestinian Americans affected by settler attacks, and again described violent
settler actions as “an act of terror.” He said crimes and acts of terror
“cannot continue” without Israeli authorities investigating and prosecuting
them. Huckabee said he would exert “pressure in order to get some resolution
to things you’ve [mostly Palestinian American residents of Turmus] brought up
today.”

The September 5-6 _Times_ article reported that in June, “More than 200
prominent Israelis signed a letter…demanding that the government stop the
attacks against Palestinian civilians in the West Bank. The signatories
included two former prime ministers, more than three dozen retired Army and
Air Force generals, the former heads of the nation’s foreign and domestic
intelligence services, as well as rabbis, a Nobel laureate and one of Israel’s
most revered novelists.”

The Mepha sign has disappeared from one pharmacy car in Geneva. And the
pharmacy no longer pushes Mepha/Teva products unless there are no
alternatives. Those are small things and minuscule protests.

Should more be done?

Referring to the UK’s planned ban on trade with unlawful Israeli settlements,
Francesca Albanese, the U.N.’s special rapporteur on the occupied territories,
said in an interview with the _Guardian_ : “because the 2024 ICJ advisory
opinion declares the entire Israeli presence in the occupied territories as
unlawful, third states’ obligations not to ‘render aid or assistance’ extends
to everything that sustains that unlawful presence as a whole.”

The words of the Israeli generals who went to the West Bank are hard to
ignore. They came back talking about ethnic cleansing, the threat to Israel
and their shame at what their country was doing. And the American ambassador,
a strong supporter of Israel, calling the settlers “terrorists” and promising
to exert pressure for change is also hard to ignore.

For the moment, boycotting at the pharmacy, former military and government
officials signing a protest letter, the brave resistance by Combattants for
Peace, and even the American ambassador’s promised pressure have had no
effect. Netanyahu and his government have not budged.
